areas.area: Vibe and Build: two ways to work
areas.summary: Studio opens in Vibe, a calm front door with one box to talk or build and cards that only appear when they have something to say. Build is the full studio with every page in reach. Studio remembers which mode you use.

features.name: Vibe mode
features.what: One box for an idea, a fix or a question. Cards appear only when they have rows: Needs you, Building now, Plan in flight, Freshly done and Fresh ideas. A quiet project shows one calm line instead of empty boxes.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] Added 'Vibe mode'; [0.4.4] 'Vibe's cards and dock come and go'; renderer/booklet.template.html #vibe-layer lanes

features.name: Vibe dock and panels
features.what: The dock always has Tasks, Team and More. Watch, Plans and Ideas step in only while they matter. Each opens a compact panel beside the box: rows open their detail, Back or Esc steps out, and Full view opens the full page without leaving Vibe.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'Vibe has its own menus'; docs/architecture.md 'Getting around'; booklet.template.html #vibe-dock

features.name: Vibe stays Vibe
features.what: Pages you open from Vibe (Tasks, Plans, Agents, Command, Settings, Search results) open inside Vibe's own narrow rail. The way back is always at the top, and the Build switch is the only way out.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Vibe mode stays Vibe'; docs/architecture.md 'Nothing you click in Vibe mode leaves it'

features.name: Build mode
features.what: The full studio: the Home workspace plus the Work and Agents pages. Switch from the top of Vibe, from the foot of Vibe's rail, from Settings › General › Studio mode, or with 'Switch to Build' in Search.
features.evidence: README.md 'Vibe or Build'; docs/architecture.md 'Getting around'; renderer/vibe.js registers 'Switch to Build'

features.name: Your workspace (Home, H)
features.what: The Build home screen. It holds the conversation with Chat and Create task, the current task (its worker, action, checks and next step) and Your work (All, Queue, Ideas, Review, Done). Studio status tiles cover workers, Needs you, Up next, the machine and today's usage.
features.evidence: README.md 'Your workspace (H)'; docs/architecture.md 'Workspace and work'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Redesigned Home around a bottom composer'

features.name: Home over the live tree
features.what: Home's panels are frosted glass, with the live node tree drifting behind them as scenery. Turning off Blur behind panels makes them solid.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Home is glass over the live node tree'

features.name: App preview
features.what: Studio can start your project's own local preview from a root index.html or a dev/start script. It then offers Open app and Stop preview. Preview state is separate from whether an agent is working or the task is verified.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Project previews have their own Start, Open and Stop'; docs/architecture.md 'App preview'

features.name: Open Vibe on launch
features.what: Choose whether Studio opens on Vibe or on Watch (the live node tree). You can change Studio mode without leaving Settings.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Settings › General gains a Studio mode switch'; renderer/vibe-panels.js 'Open Vibe on launch'

features.name: What's new card
features.what: A one-time card, 'Two ways to work: Vibe and Build', offers Try Vibe, Keep Build and a link to the full changelog.
features.evidence: renderer/booklet.template.html #vibe-notes (present in v0.4.2)

features.name: A first run with no AI says so
features.what: With nothing connected, Home, Vibe and the agent status read 'No AI connected' and show a Connect an AI button. Start agents says which coding tool to install instead of failing five times.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'A first run with no AI connected says so'; commit 6a5c7be

areas.summary: Describe what you want in plain words. Talk it over with Mefi, or press Build it: Studio decides whether it is one task or a short plan of steps and puts it on the board. The chat can also act on your tasks when you ask plainly.

features.name: Talk it over
features.what: Chat with Mefi about an idea without creating any work (Enter in Vibe's box). From 0.4.5, describing something buildable gets a reply that offers the board instead of filing a task quietly.
features.evidence: booklet.template.html #vibe-talk, hint 'Enter to talk · Ctrl + Enter to build'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Talk it over talks'

features.name: Build it
features.what: Press Build it (Ctrl+Enter) to turn your words into work on the board. If the agents are off, paused or have no AI, it says so and points at the control that starts them.
features.evidence: booklet.template.html #vibe-build; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] Fixed 'Build it no longer promises the task will start'

features.name: Mefi sizes it
features.what: A short, single change goes straight onto the board. For a bigger request, the lead agent may split it into two to six steps that each leave the project working, and your own card runs last as the final check.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'Mefi sizes it'; docs/architecture.md 'Build it sizes the request'; scripts/request-sizing.cjs

features.name: Plan in flight and Make it one task
features.what: A split request shows as a Plan in flight card with its progress. When approval is needed, its waiting steps are one row you start together. Make it one task drops the steps that have not started.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Mefi sizes it'; renderer/vibe-panels.js 'Start all steps', 'Make it one task'

features.name: Watch Mefi think
features.what: Suggest a next step and Build it show a live strip instead of one still sentence. It shows the stage reached, the files read or steps planned as they arrive, which model is thinking, and a clock against how long this usually takes on your PC.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Watch Mefi think, and watch your team work'; renderer/vibe-flow.js; commit b92b482

features.name: Watch your team on a split request
features.what: The plan card draws its steps as a track that ends in the final check. It names the step being built, its agent's tool and what the agent is doing now. Building now rows and the Plans panel timeline show the same.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Watch Mefi think'; docs/architecture.md 'The agent team on a split request'

features.name: MEFI: Modify, Experiment, Fix, Improve
features.what: Four starting points for changing the open project, Studio itself included. Pick an approach, describe the change, then talk it over or build it. The choice stays with that project's draft.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Build on your app with MEFI'; renderer/vibe.js modify/experiment/fix/improve; commit 75de5a4

features.name: Suggest a next step
features.what: Mefi reads your project and suggests next steps with reasons and file references. Add to draft appends an editable brief, Save idea keeps a suggestion for later and Clear puts the set away. Nothing starts until you build.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Suggestions stay usable'; docs/architecture.md 'MEFI — Modify, Experiment, Fix, Improve'

features.name: New app
features.what: Use the + beside Vibe's project picker: name an app and say what it should be. Studio makes a fresh folder under Mefi Apps, starts git, opens the folder and sends your description through Build it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'New app'; docs/architecture.md 'New app'

features.name: Chat and Create task
features.what: Home's composer has Chat for discussion and Create task for work with acceptance checks. Use a task outline adds room for the goal, the checks and the boundaries, and Plan an idea opens Plans.
features.evidence: README.md 'What it does'; GETTING_STARTED.md §3; booklet.template.html 'Use a task outline', 'Plan an idea'

features.name: Add files
features.what: Drop text or code files into Home, Vibe or Plans, or use Add files, to put their contents into your draft as editable text (up to eight files, 128 KB each). A drop never sends a message or approves anything.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Drop text and code files into Home, Vibe and Plans'; docs/architecture.md intro

features.name: Drafts kept per project
features.what: Chat, task and Vibe drafts are saved separately for each project and survive navigation.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Vibe keeps project-specific drafts'; GETTING_STARTED.md §3

features.name: Chat that acts on your tasks
features.what: Ask your companion to start, retry or stop a task, mark it done, leave a note for the next worker or file new work. Anything you did not plainly ask for becomes a card for you to confirm. Plain phrases such as 'stop the auth build' work even without an AI key.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The assistant you chat with oversees the work'; scripts/task-oversight.cjs (first in v0.4.0)

features.name: Task updates in the conversation
features.what: Each task gets one line in the thread that updates in place: started, verifying, verified, retrying, parked. Cards only you can move are rolled into one 'needs you' line.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The assistant and the agent loop'

features.name: A companion that knows where you are
features.what: Replies use the name you gave your companion and know which screen you are on. After it offers several cards, saying 'all of them' or 'both' starts exactly those, and the offers also appear as one-tap buttons.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Your companion knows where you are and what is waiting'

features.name: Companion bubble menu
features.what: Click the companion or press Esc to open its menu. In 0.4.5 the menu becomes six bubbles with one job each: Talk (with What are you doing?, What's next? and Recap today), What I'm doing, Needs you, Suggest work, Friends and Personality. The bubble menu itself has existed since 0.4.0.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'The companion as a pet and a friend'; [0.4.0] 'A glowing wisp… bubble menu'; docs/architecture.md 'Click the companion'

features.name: Suggest work
features.what: From the companion, send your own idea to the inbox, or pick one of its next suggestions from the backlog with Work on it. Nothing starts on its own.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Suggest work takes the owner's idea into the inbox'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]

features.name: Welcome back digest
features.what: After ten or more minutes away, or when the PC wakes, the companion tells you what finished, what stopped and what needs you.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Agent Brain 'Your companion lives in the menu foot'; docs/architecture.md 'The companion in the menu foot'

features.name: Automatic task context
features.what: New tasks gather matching code, session and chat references by themselves. A small scout model can then pick a checked starting file for the builder.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'New tasks gather local code, session and chat context automatically'; docs/architecture.md glossary 'Task'

areas.summary: When the route is unclear, Plans interviews you until the idea becomes a specification you approve, then turns it into tasks. Ideas collect in an inbox and only become work when you say so.

features.name: Plans (P): the interview
features.what: Describe the outcome, and Mefi asks the question that would most change what gets built. It reads your answer back, flags contradictions and follows what you said into the next question. Every line is labelled by who said it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] Changed 'Plans leads with an interview'; docs/architecture.md 'Planning'

features.name: What we understand
features.what: Before any specification is drafted, Mefi reads the plan back to you and waits for your confirmation. Changing the destination or any decision withdraws it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'A specification waits for What we understand'; docs/architecture.md 'Planning'

features.name: From specification to tasks
features.what: Write or request a specification with small tasks, acceptance checks and prerequisites, approve it, then create its tasks when you choose. Planning never launches workers, and manual planning works without an AI key.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Planning'; GETTING_STARTED.md §3

features.name: Write with Mefi
features.what: A live writing partner explores your project files as you type and shows what it found. It offers wording you can edit, Refine for a single field and Undo. Write manually turns it off.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Plans gains a live AI writing partner'; docs/architecture.md 'Planning'

features.name: Continue with Mefi
features.what: Your answer is saved before Mefi is asked. A failed reply loses nothing, and Continue with Mefi resumes the interview without filing your answer twice.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] Fixed 'Plans: a failed Mefi reply'

features.name: Archive and Restore plan
features.what: Set a plan aside, read-only, under Show archived, and bring it back exactly as it was.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Plans: Archive plan and Restore plan'

features.name: Continue where you left off
features.what: Plans remembers the selected plan and stage for each project. Planning reads fresh project excerpts plus any files you name.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Plans restore the last selected plan'; docs/architecture.md intro

features.name: Plan timeline in Vibe
features.what: Vibe's Plans panel shows a plan as a timeline: who is on each step, and which step each waiting one waits for.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'the plan panel's new timeline'; docs/architecture.md 'The agent team on a split request'

features.name: Feature ideas (I)
features.what: An unread idea inbox and a feature graph. Ideas become tasks only when you or Work through backlog promote them. Scan chats for ideas collects new ones from recent conversations.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md glossary 'Idea'; renderer/nav.js 'Feature ideas' (I), 'Scan chats for ideas'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Feature ideas shows each idea's title, source and state'

features.name: First map ideas
features.what: The walkthrough's First map explores your folder read-only and saves its suggested first tasks as ideas, never as tasks. It can run through a subscription CLI login.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md 'The walkthrough'; docs/cli-setup.md 'Mapping on a subscription'

features.name: Fresh ideas in Vibe
features.what: New ideas appear on a Fresh ideas card and in the Ideas panel. From there you can build each one, keep it for later or dismiss it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'the new Fresh ideas card'; renderer/vibe-panels.js 'Keep for later', 'Dismiss'

features.name: Work through backlog
features.what: Works through the project's existing tasks and ideas first, admitting ideas in small batches while keeping a small buffer of ready work.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Work through backlog'; GETTING_STARTED.md §4

areas.summary: Every piece of work is a task with a brief, acceptance checks, prerequisites, attempts and evidence. You can follow it from Ready to Working to Review to Done and step in at any point.

features.name: Task board (T)
features.what: Plan cards with progress and a current step. Each task holds its brief, prerequisites, hand-off context and history, and the board filters by scheduling state.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The task board'; renderer/nav.js 'Task board' key T

features.name: Plain task states
features.what: Ready, Awaiting build approval, Working, Waiting on prerequisites, Retry scheduled, Needs attention, Awaiting verification and Done, each with the next step to take.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md §4 table; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'One status vocabulary'

features.name: Prerequisites
features.what: Choose which tasks must finish before this one can start. Missing prerequisites and dependency loops are flagged so you can fix them.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The task board'; renderer/tasks.js 'Save prerequisites'

features.name: Live worker status
features.what: Running cards show whether the worker is preparing, building, finishing or stopping. They also show its current step or tool, the builder route and how long ago it last updated.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Home and Command now show a worker's current step'; docs/architecture.md 'Running task cards'

features.name: Start this task
features.what: Start or resume one task by itself, even while the queue is paused. Approval, prerequisites and machine limits still apply, and the result names any hold.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Start this task and confirmed chat starts'; docs/architecture.md 'Start this task'

features.name: Task run history
features.what: A task lists each attempt: who ran it, how it ended and what it changed.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Task run history'

features.name: Brief history
features.what: Load earlier versions of a task's brief and restore one if a change went the wrong way.
features.evidence: renderer/tasks.js 'Load earlier briefs', 'Restore this brief' (present in v0.2.0)

features.name: Notes for the next attempt
features.what: Leave a note on a task, including a queued one in Vibe, and the next worker reads it first.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'A queued task takes a note for its next attempt'; renderer/vibe-panels.js 'Tell it something for its next attempt…'

features.name: Drop and Reopen
features.what: Close a task you won't do without marking it done. The task that handed it on stops waiting for it, and Reopen brings it back.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Fixed 'Drop closes a task you won't do'

features.name: Waiting on follow-ups
features.what: A task that handed work on reads 'Waiting on follow-ups' and finishes by itself, so only the stuck follow-up asks for you.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Fixed 'The Review list shows only work that needs you'

features.name: Request a change, View checks, Open app
features.what: Finished work offers these beside its preview. Request a change opens a new, linked task draft and keeps the original task's evidence.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Completed work offers View checks and Request a change'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Completed tasks expose Open app'

features.name: Copy handoff and done summary
features.what: Copy a task's hand-off to pass to another worker, or its done summary to share.
features.evidence: renderer/tasks.js 'Copy handoff', 'Copy the done summary'

features.name: Vibe Tasks: List and Lanes
features.what: Switch between a list and lanes (Needs you, Ready, Building, Checking, Later, Done) with live counts. The panel also has pause and resume and a worker limit of 1, 2, 3 or Automatic.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Vibe Tasks gains List/Lanes'; [Unreleased] 'Vibe's worker limit offers only what the host honours'; docs/architecture.md 'Vibe's Tasks panel'

features.name: Task inspector
features.what: Save a task's priority, estimated minutes, Done when checks and a Defer until date. Return to queue clears a deferral. From 0.4.5, deferred work reads 'Scheduled for later' with its reason.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Its Inspector saves task priority'; docs/architecture.md 'Each task's Inspector'; [Unreleased] 'Scheduled for later'

features.name: Work on it
features.what: Make any task, session or node Mefi's next piece of work. It is pinned to the front of the board and started right away.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Work on it makes a node the assistant's next piece of work'

features.name: Swarm or Cluster
features.what: Swarm gives each ready task its own builder across the queue. Cluster puts planning, review and scoped delegation around one shared task.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md glossary 'Swarm / Cluster'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Default Swarm dispatch uses one builder per task'

features.name: Parallel builds
features.what: Machine managed starts builds while the app stays responsive and backs off when the PC is busy. You can also set a manual limit of one to three workers.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Parallel builds defaults to Machine managed'; booklet.template.html 'Parallel builds'

features.name: Projects and Save & switch
features.what: Each folder keeps its own tasks, conversations, plans and references. Switching while a worker runs stops it, saves its progress and waits for the save before opening the other project.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Projects keeps each folder's tasks'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Fixed 'Save & switch waits for saved progress'

areas.summary: Choose who answers and who builds. Studio works with the AI you already have: a Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity login, an API key, or a local model. Coding CLIs do the building, while a team of helper agents organises, reviews and writes briefs.

features.name: Agents workspace
features.what: One place for your team: Overview, Setup, Live, Workflows, Models and Usage, with start and pause controls and a list of what needs you.
features.evidence: docs/unified-studio.md 'Agents' table; renderer/agents.js (first in v0.4.0)

features.name: Setup helper
features.what: One menu for every setting that decides what agents do: Connect an AI, Team & models, Routing, How work runs, Permissions, Tools & skills, Machine & app and Look. Quick setup takes three steps, and the helper opens first on a new install.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Setup helper'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'First: the setup helper'; renderer/setup-helper.js (absent from v0.4.4); commit 9cb13e2

features.name: Connect an AI
features.what: Choose Set up automatically, Start free with OpenCode, or a signed-in login, API key, LM Studio or custom endpoint. A coding tool that is installed but not signed in is marked as such and no longer counts as connected.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Setup finds the login you have'; docs/architecture.md 'setup helper'

features.name: Guided CLI install and sign-in
features.what: Install and sign in to Codex, Claude Code, Grok, Antigravity or OpenCode from a visible setup window, then Check connection. Use for the whole studio routes chat, planning, agents and coding through that one subscription.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Added 'Guided CLI installation, sign-in and connection checks'; docs/cli-setup.md

features.name: Auto setup
features.what: Reads the keys, CLIs and local servers already on your PC (Ollama included) and applies a matching setup in one pass, without sending any paid request. A fresh install runs it by itself.
features.evidence: README.md 'First launch' step 3; docs/architecture.md 'Auto setup'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Run auto setup'

features.name: More than one login
features.what: Add up to six Claude Code or Codex subscription logins. Work goes to the first login that has not hit its limit, and when one hits its usage limit, work moves to the next without costing the task an attempt. Usage shows one row per login.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'More than one Claude Code or Codex login'; docs/cli-setup.md 'More than one login'; commit 07150aa

features.name: Team & models
features.what: Each agent gets a model menu, effort and fast settings, and a provider icon. Refresh model list fetches the provider's current models, and you can always type a model ID.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Agent setup now uses compact model rows'; docs/unified-studio.md

features.name: Team presets and project teams
features.what: Save a team as a preset, apply it to a project as an independent copy, and keep Studio defaults that new projects inherit. Edits wait for Apply changes or Discard draft.
features.evidence: docs/unified-studio.md 'Team configuration uses Apply changes and Discard draft'; renderer/agents.js 'Save as new preset'

features.name: Agent seats
features.what: Named seats, each on its own model: the lead (plans and splits work), the desk (helps stuck workers), your companion (talks with you), the scout (finds a starting file), the overseer (reviews the team) and the subtask builders.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Seats' and 'Agents setup now includes companion, scout, overseer and subtask routing'; renderer/agents.js role descriptions

features.name: Helper roles you can see
features.what: An always-on loop of small roles keeps the board tidy: watcher, machine, auditor, keeper, thinker, briefer, responder, foreman, compactor, overseer and scout. They leave each other notes you can read under 'Said to each other'.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md glossary 'Agent roles', 'Agent mail'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Agent mail'

features.name: Vibe Team panel
features.what: Shows who is building and which model each seat runs, in plain words ('Talks with you', 'Plans the work', 'Builds your code', 'Helps stuck agents'), with Start, Resume or Pause. From 0.4.5 it also lists what Mefi is thinking about now.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Team shows who is building and which model each seat runs on'; renderer/vibe-panels.js; [Unreleased] 'Team lists what Mefi is thinking about'

features.name: Skills per agent
features.what: The + on an agent attaches up to eight installed local skills (SKILL.md folders from .claude, .codex, .agents or OpenCode skill folders) to that agent only.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'a left-side + for per-agent local skills'; docs/unified-studio.md; docs/agent-tools.md

features.name: Web search, project reads and MCP tools
features.what: For each agent, turn on web search, read-only project file reads and up to sixteen tools from MCP servers you trust. Builders get these through a per-run tool attachment.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Per-agent web search, project-read permissions and MCP tool allowlists'; docs/agent-tools.md

features.name: Habits
features.what: Short behaviour rules for each agent: explain changes, test, take small steps, match the code around it, report shape and a to-do list. Each can be off, brief or full, and Studio shows the tokens they add to every prompt.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Habits'; scripts/habits.cjs (absent from v0.4.4 tree, restored by dc85f68)

features.name: Model routing
features.what: Auto works down a provider list you can reorder, trying signed-in coding CLIs first unless you turn that off, with optional fallback. You can also pin z.ai, OpenCode Go or Zen, OpenRouter, a CLI login, LM Studio or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Heavy and routine answers can go to different providers.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'AI routing picks who pays'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'Planning and reading can each answer through their own provider'; [0.4.0] 'OpenRouter as a companion provider'

features.name: Failing routes pause themselves
features.what: After three failures in a row, a provider is paused briefly and the next one answers straight away. Saving a key or changing routing lifts the pause.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Changed 'A model route that keeps failing is paused instead of retried every turn'

features.name: Jev decision model
features.what: An optional classifier model, reached through Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe, OpenCode Zen or OpenRouter, that helps pick models. Without it Studio uses fixed defaults.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Settings › Decision model'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'Jev model selection'

features.name: Coding CLIs as builders
features.what: OpenCode (preferred), Claude Code, Codex, Grok or Antigravity edit your files using your own logins. A CLI that never gets going falls back once to OpenCode when OpenCode is installed.
features.evidence: README.md 'What it does'; docs/architecture.md 'Builders run through opencode run'

features.name: Coding tiers
features.what: Auto, Free, Fast or Heavy decide what each build may cost. Settings shows which model each tier resolves to before anything runs.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'coding tiers (Auto / Free / Fast / Heavy)'; docs/architecture.md 'A coding tier'

features.name: Learns which model wins
features.what: Under the Auto tier, the checker scores every build as a win or a loss. The model most likely to succeed, weighing cost, speed and remaining allowance, builds next.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'coding tier' (win probability, agent-loop.md §12); win-probability code first appears in v0.4.0 main.cjs and scripts/executor-core.cjs

features.name: Try again with a heavier model
features.what: A one-tap retry that runs the next attempt on the builder's Heavy-tier model. From 0.4.5 it really uses that model and is offered only where one exists.
features.evidence: docs/brain-maps.md 'retry-deep'; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Try again with a heavier model runs the Heavy-tier model'

features.name: Every builder checked the same way
features.what: Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity builds are checked by Studio's own verification instead of parking with 'retry it on OpenCode', and Codex builders get Studio's tools.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'First-time setup and agent choice… Any builder'

features.name: Ask the desk mid-run
features.what: With Let workers ask the desk on, OpenCode and Claude Code workers can ask the desk agent a question through a local tool and wait for its answer. Off by default.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Give workers the ask_desk tool'; main.cjs agentBrain.deskTool defaults false

features.name: Nested delegation and head drafts
features.what: Two switches, off by default. One lets a delegated slice split once more (never past three levels). The other lets the lead draft a pipeline for a complex task that no recipe fits.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Nested delegation (off by default)', 'Head drafts (off by default)'; renderer/agents.js 'Allow nested delegation', 'Draft complex pipelines'

features.name: Per-session worktree runs
features.what: Opt-in. Each build gets its own git checkout and branch, which merge back one run at a time, so parallel runs never trip over each other.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Builders can run in per-session worktrees' (MEFI_STUDIO_WORKTREE_RUNS=1)

areas.summary: The Command view draws your project as a live node tree. Every session, task and agent is a node, and agents fly to the work they are doing and say what they are up to in speech bubbles.

features.name: Command view (D)
features.what: Sessions, tasks and agents as a live node tree in 2D or 3D. Agents orbit the assistant, fly to the task they are working on and bring finished work home.
features.evidence: README.md 'Command view (D)'; docs/architecture.md glossary 'Command view'

features.name: Speech bubbles and agent notes
features.what: Bubbles beside each agent say what it is doing. Findings going home and notes between agents ride the lines as small packets.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Speech bubbles beside the agents'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Agent mail'

features.name: Callouts and focus
features.what: Sessions, tasks and working agents carry numbered cards (S1, T4…) with done and remaining counts. Click one and the camera glides in while the rest of the tree keeps turning behind a blur.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Sessions, tasks, the assistant and working agents carry a callout'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'numbered callouts, click-to-focus camera'

features.name: Agent glyphs and motion
features.what: Each agent wears its role glyph (an eye for the watcher, a hammer for a builder, a crown for the overseer). It spins a ring while working and leaves a coloured trail when it flies.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Every agent wears its role glyph'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'agent glyphs'

features.name: Absorb
features.what: A finished node collapses into the node it belongs to, and its brief stays readable under Absorbed work.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'the absorb animation for finished work'; docs/architecture.md 'The Runs tab'

features.name: Lines that mean something
features.what: The hub link is doubled, a task's anchor marches while its worker runs, an agent's tether is dashed, a finished cluster is stippled and a done to-do's link fades green.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Lines say what they mean'

features.name: Inspect mode
features.what: Selecting a node gives its details the whole right panel at full height, while every other control moves back to its edge. Esc steps out one level at a time.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Inspect mode in Command view'; docs/architecture.md 'Inspect mode'

features.name: Work, Assistant, Runs and Ask panels
features.what: Work shows the current worker and step, readiness counts, the roster and a ranked queue. Assistant is the chat log, with one-tap Status, What next?, Log, Help, Oversee, Tidy and Fix. Runs groups recent builds by task, and Ask holds decisions with a recommended option.
features.evidence: README.md 'Command view (D)'; docs/architecture.md 'Live work'; booklet.template.html Command rail ('Recent runs' first in v0.4.0)

features.name: Command toolbar
features.what: Four groups: Agents (Swarm or Cluster, plus a dropdown of queue controls), Camera (Fit, Overview or Follow, Spin), View (2D or 3D, Labels, Zoom) and Sound.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'The Command toolbar is four labelled groups'; [0.4.0] 'Command's agent settings now open from the top toolbar's Agents dropdown'

features.name: Labels
features.what: Cycle between Auto, Updates, All and None with L. Updates shows task progress and reported code changes without routine agent chatter.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Command's node labels now include Updates'; docs/architecture.md 'View › Labels'

features.name: Layouts and 3D Overview
features.what: Five arrangements, chosen per project: Constellation, Branches, Rings, Helix and Terraces, in 2D or real 3D. The 3D Overview turns the tree in place and drifts gently to keep all of it in view.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Follow frames the active task'; CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Command's automatic 3D Overview now gently pans'

features.name: Node styles
features.what: Eight looks that all animate: Classic orbs, Soft glass, Minimal, Halo and Crystal, plus the Void collection's Singularity, Prism and Sigil. All are free.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Remastered node styles'; [0.4.4] 'The Void collection is free'

features.name: Skies and card style
features.what: Themed skies (Aurora, Deep space, Nebula, Rising embers, Fireflies, Soft bokeh, Warm dust) or a plain backdrop. Speech bubbles can be switched on or off, and cards can be outlined, filled or auto.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The sky follows the colour theme'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'themed skies'

features.name: Zen tour
features.what: Park the mouse at the right edge and the camera tours the tree while the panels fade. Move, click or type to come back. An idle Zen setting and Zen bells are also available.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.3] 'Parking the mouse at the right edge'; docs/architecture.md 'Zen / demo flight'; booklet.template.html 'Zen bells'

features.name: Touch, pinch and keys
features.what: The wheel or a two-finger pinch zooms toward the pointer, and touch and pen work like the mouse. [ and ] step through tasks, C cycles the camera, V switches 2D and 3D, and Space pauses the spin.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Interaction: the wheel and a two-finger pinch'; booklet.template.html button titles (C, Space, L, V)

features.name: The tree moves to music and video
features.what: With the audio link on, music can speed up the spin and make the tree sway and swell. Tree modes choose Steady, Music, Video or both, with ring, wave or spiral shapes and controls for brightness and outlines.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Tree motion'; [0.4.3] 'Tree modes & movement', 'brightness sliders'

features.name: Legend and Usage pill
features.what: Corner pop-ups explain the tree's symbols and show your plan usage at a glance.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'The Usage popover covers every provider'; docs/architecture.md 'Usage popover'

features.name: Command view after 5 quiet minutes
features.what: The automatic jump to Command view after five quiet minutes becomes a switch, off by default.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'No more surprise jump to Command view'

features.name: Overhead (O)
features.what: The node tree seen from above with task boxes, showing which session is working on which task.
features.evidence: renderer/nav.js 'Overhead' key O; docs/architecture.md glossary 'Session'

areas.area: Agent brain, Playbook and project map
areas.summary: See how a task is broken into steps and who is working each one. Studio remembers the recipes that worked, and a map of your project's systems shows where work happens.

features.name: Agent brain (J)
features.what: Draws one task's pipeline top-down: your companion as the head, then the lead, the steps and the sub-agents working them. Sub-agents go out, pop when done, fly home and are absorbed, and their reports climb the tree.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'The Agent Brain'; docs/architecture.md 'The Agent Brain'

features.name: Replay today
features.what: Play back the day's recorded agent events.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Replay today plays back the day's recorded events'

features.name: Pipelines
features.what: Every task gets a plan of steps before its worker starts, taken from the best saved recipe or a template. The plan grows from the worker's own to-do list and folds finished steps away.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Every task gets a pipeline'; docs/architecture.md 'A task's pipeline'

features.name: Reports up the tree
features.what: A delegated sub-agent's report reaches its parent, and a finished child starts the parent's integration pass at once.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Sub-agents report up the tree'

features.name: The desk
features.what: A desk agent answers stuck workers' questions on the lead's model and folds repeated questions together. It sends you only what it cannot answer.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'The desk worker answers stuck workers'

features.name: Playbook
features.what: Every verified or failed pipeline is filed as a recipe, and the next task of the same kind starts from the recipe that succeeds most. Pin, rename, retire or delete recipes on a shelf where thickness shows runs and colour shows success.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'The Playbook'; docs/architecture.md 'Agent brain (J) draws it'

features.name: Seats tab
features.what: See and change the models behind the lead and desk seats (GPT 6 Sol via OpenCode Zen by default), plus the delegation switches.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Seats: the lead and the desk run GPT 6 Sol'; renderer/agent-brain.js 'Agent seats'

features.name: Project map
features.what: A map of your project's systems, built from recent git history and the files that verified runs touched. Large folders split into groups of files that change together, and systems link by shared history. Workers are told the related systems and the files that change most.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'The project map'; docs/architecture.md 'Project map, under Agents › Workflows'

features.name: Explore the map
features.what: Click to inspect and double-click to go inside. Back and Forward, breadcrumbs, Browse (search every file, with All, Working and Changed filters) and a clickable minimap help you move around.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Project map exploration now has Back/Forward'; docs/unified-studio.md 'Navigation and overflow'

features.name: Name the systems
features.what: Ask the lead agent to give the map's systems readable names.
features.evidence: docs/roadmap-0.4.0.md M7 'naming by the lead seat on demand'; renderer/agent-brain.js 'Asking the lead to name the systems…'

features.name: Project map on Home
features.what: Pick a system beside the conversation to see its tasks, ideas and plans, then choose Work on this region. You can place ideas and plans on a system, and Work here drafts a task for a system, part or file.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'Home shows the project map'; docs/roadmap-0.4.0.md M8; renderer/project-map-view.js 'Work here', 'Copy path' (in v0.4.0)

features.name: Connected system cards
features.what: Systems that changed together share a branch with their parts and files. Systems without that evidence wait under Connections still to discover.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'A map that shows relationships'; docs/architecture.md 'Project map'

features.name: Ideas tree
features.what: Groups your ideas and tasks by system and progress. It keeps ideas under their tasks and subtasks under their parents, and regroups as agents discover files.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'The separate Ideas tree'; renderer/project-map-view.js (no Ideas tree in v0.4.4); commit 75de5a4

features.name: Work with Mefi from the map
features.what: The map inspector's Modify, Experiment, Fix and Improve buttons prepare a Vibe draft about the chosen area.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Work with Mefi prepares a contextual Vibe draft'

areas.summary: Studio notices what changed in your folder while it was closed, including commits you made by hand and other coding agents you ran, and checks queued work against it before building anything twice.

features.name: While Studio was away
features.what: Studio keeps a last look at each folder. When you return it reports the commits, uncommitted edits and Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode sessions run there in the meantime.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Work done outside Studio'; docs/architecture.md glossary; scripts/outside-work.cjs

features.name: Queued work is checked first
features.what: If the code changed, each queued card is checked against that work. A card that is still needed runs as before, and a partly done one runs with its worker told what changed. A card that looks already done waits for you with Mark it done, Drop it or Build it anyway.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Work done outside Studio'; renderer/tasks.js 'Build it anyway', 'Looks already done outside Studio.'

features.name: Evidence tab verdict
features.what: The task's Evidence tab shows the verdict and the commits behind it.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Work done outside Studio… The task's Evidence tab shows the verdict'

features.name: Ask what changed, even without AI
features.what: Ask 'what did I do while Studio was closed?' and the chat answers from the report even with no model connected. When a card matched only by file and commit names, it says the work 'may already be done'.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Asking what changed while you were away works without a model'; commit d85ece8

areas.summary: An agent saying it is done is not enough. Finished work waits with its evidence until your project's own checks pass or you confirm it yourself.

features.name: Awaiting verification
features.what: A finished attempt waits with its evidence until the checks pass or you confirm it. When evidence is not available yet, the task waits without losing a retry.
features.evidence: README.md '"Done" means verified'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Verification stage'

features.name: Your project's own checks
features.what: Checks run in the task's own folder using its check or test script, a root tests file or its LÖVE harness. They never borrow Studio's own checks.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Changed 'Verification checks stay in the dispatched task's project'; docs/architecture.md 'Verification, storage and experiments'

features.name: Review
features.what: Review lists only work that needs you: finished runs waiting for checks and attempts that need attention.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Fixed 'The Review list shows only work that needs you'; renderer/tasks.js

features.name: Mark done
features.what: After reviewing a result yourself, you can mark it complete. The board keeps 'Completion verified' separate from 'Completion confirmed by you'.
features.evidence: renderer/tasks.js 'Mark done', 'Completion confirmed by you', 'Completion verified'

features.name: Honest retries
features.what: A retry is judged by its own check, never by an earlier attempt's pass. Its note quotes the failing command so the next worker sees it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Fixed 'A retry is no longer verified by an earlier attempt's check'

features.name: Rate recent work
features.what: Give your own score to a result you reviewed. It stays separate from model judging and error counts.
features.evidence: booklet.template.html Model Lab 'Rate recent work' (present in v0.2.0)

areas.summary: You decide how much Mefi handles for you. Everything that needs you is in one list, every automatic choice comes with a reason and Undo, and one switch pauses everything.

features.name: Needs you
features.what: One list of everything waiting on you (questions, builds waiting for your OK and stuck tasks), with the same count on the companion, the menu badge and the tray.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] 'keeps one queue of everything that needs you… the count in the tray'; Changed '"Requests", "what needs me" and the badge now mean one list'

features.name: Ask cards with a recommended option
features.what: Agent questions arrive as cards showing the task, the failing check and the last lines the agent saw, with options that act on that task. A toast with an Answer button reaches you from any view.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'A decision lane for agent issues', 'A new agent question raises a toast with an Answer button'

features.name: Answer in Vibe
features.what: Answer opens a drawer with the question, the task it blocks and its options (recommended first), or takes your own words, then moves on to the next item. Builds waiting for approval show their brief, and stuck tasks offer Try again, Resume or Run anyway, It's done and Drop it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Vibe: answer decisions without leaving it', 'Vibe can run on its own'; docs/architecture.md 'Answer on a decision under Needs you'

features.name: What holds the agents
features.what: A banner names whatever is holding every agent back and carries the fix: Start agents, Resume or Connect an AI. 0.4.5 adds Try now, Restart Studio and Open a project.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.2] 'Vibe can run on its own'; docs/architecture.md 'Vibe can run on its own'

features.name: Agents say why they are not working
features.what: Home, Vibe, Command, the Agents switches, each task and the chat all read one shared answer about what is holding work back and which control clears it, so they never disagree.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Agents say why they are not working'; scripts/loop-status.cjs; commit 1d86a1a

features.name: Permission modes
features.what: Always ask, Accept per task, Auto (the default) or Elevated only decide how much Mefi handles for you. From 0.4.5 each mode says what happens to a new task, and the old Auto build switch no longer overwrites your mode.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Four saved permission modes'; renderer/autonomy-ui.js MODES; [Unreleased] 'Permission modes keep their meaning'

features.name: Elevated requests
features.what: Six kinds of decision stay yours unless you switch them off: granting reach, irreversible changes, closing your work, work agents propose, a pricier model and real-world to-dos. Switching off either of the first two needs a warning acknowledged.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Six elevated categories'; scripts/autonomy.cjs ELEVATED

features.name: Permission chip
features.what: The same permission control appears in the composer, Vibe Settings, the companion, Agents Overview and Search, and all of them share one saved setting.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Mefi's permission chip… share one saved state'; docs/architecture.md 'Permission modes'

features.name: Decided for you, with Why and Undo
features.what: Every automatic choice is listed with its reason. Undo reopens the question, waits for any running worker and keeps your later edits.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Automatic answers have a bounded decision history with reasons and Undo'; booklet.template.html 'Decided for you · For you'

features.name: Mefi decided
features.what: Answers Mefi gives for you are labelled 'Mefi decided' with a reason. They keep your stops and each card's retry limits, and they are never learned as your preference.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] Fixed 'Such answers are now marked "Mefi decided"'

features.name: For you list
features.what: Real-world to-dos that only a person can do go on a short list, where you can mark each one Done or Not mine.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Real-world leftovers become a short For you list'; renderer/autonomy-ui.js 'Not mine'

features.name: Learns from your answers
features.what: Mefi learns from your answers, with recent choices counting more and corrections counting double. Learning can cover this project, all projects or a blend. You can see what it learned, forget one pattern or all of them, or switch learning off.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Mefi learns from successful owner answers'; docs/architecture.md 'Learning'

features.name: Approve build
features.what: When a task waits for approval, read its brief, files and prerequisites, then choose Approve build. Editing the scope asks again. From 0.4.5, approvals also survive the references gathered after them.
features.evidence: GETTING_STARTED.md §3; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Approvals survive the references gathered after them'

features.name: Things only you can do
features.what: Jobs only you can do reach you once, with I'll take care of it, Answer it in one line or Leave it for review, instead of turning into new cards that ask again.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Owner asks'; docs/brain-maps.md 'owner is for something only you can do'

features.name: Repeat questions fold
features.what: If another card asks the same question within a day, it waits on the open card or takes your earlier answer. Cards that look like the same work become one decision: keep the oldest, or keep them all.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Repeat questions fold', 'Duplicate card families become one owner decision'

features.name: Loop guard
features.what: A card that keeps failing for its own reasons is held with an explanation of why and how to fix it, and Try again releases it. Work that keeps repeating is put to you once.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'Loop guard and memory alignment'; [0.3.3] 'Owner controls for the loop guard', 'Repeating work is put to you once'

features.name: Let the desk handle asks
features.what: Off by default. When on, your companion answers open questions and restarts parked cards using the desk agent's model, then says what it chose. Permission, risk and owner-only questions always wait for you. Clear list takes stuck items off your list.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'The desk can handle asks for you'; renderer/agents.js 'Let the desk handle asks'

features.name: A tidy Needs you
features.what: Answered questions leave the list at once. Questions past their age, or whose card left the board, close when the project loads.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Answered asks leave the Needs you list', 'No dead asks after a restart'; commit e53a572

features.name: Ask twice before it can't be undone
features.what: Stop all, Restart, killing a run, dropping a task, deleting a preset, draft or recipe, Forget all and similar actions share one two-step button: the first press asks, the second acts.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Actions that can't be undone ask twice'; commit 049904c

features.name: Pause, New work and Stop all
features.what: Pause holds all new work while running jobs finish, and New work is the master switch for starting anything. Stop all halts every agent and saves its progress, and Restart Studio relaunches with agents paused.
features.evidence: README.md 'Studio at a glance… single Pause / Resume'; booklet.template.html Agents dropdown 'Stop or restart'; docs/architecture.md glossary 'Autopilot / New work'

features.name: Machine guard
features.what: Studio holds new starts when your PC gets laggy and stops stray, hung or overlong runs, logging every stop.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Machine capacity gate'; docs/architecture.md 'Machine coordination'

features.name: Keeps working in the tray
features.what: Closing the window hides Studio to the tray while agents keep working. Interrupted work resumes on the next start instead of running twice.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Closing the window hides Studio to a tray icon'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Session continuity'

features.name: Agents on several PCs claim their files
features.what: Link a cowork room to a project and builders on each of your PCs claim the files they will edit. A task whose files another PC holds waits and picks other work. This needs the rooms hub and a Discord link.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Agents on several PCs never edit the same file at once'; README.md 'Agents on several PCs'; commit c4c64de

areas.summary: The steps Studio takes from an idea to verified work, drawn as a graph you can edit. You can change which decisions reach you and see exactly which switches a map will move before it goes live.

features.name: Brain maps (B)
features.what: The agent pipeline as an editable graph of typed parts and wires. The map that ships with Studio is the loop Studio really runs.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Brain maps'; docs/brain-maps.md 'What a map is'

features.name: Make this live
features.what: Before a map goes live, the editor lists exactly which switches it will move (build approval, dispatch, briefing, Jev, model choice, workers at once) and waits for your confirmation.
features.evidence: docs/brain-maps.md 'Gates: what activating a map actually moves'

features.name: Decision lane settings
features.what: The map decides whether an agent's problem reaches you. Settings cover what Mefi may settle itself, whether repeat questions fold, how deep follow-ups may split, whether to post what changed, and when unanswered cards expire. Permission and risk questions always stay yours.
features.evidence: docs/brain-maps.md 'The decision lane'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Brain maps show what they do'

features.name: A real node editor
features.what: Pan and zoom with a minimap, drag wires from end to end, search parts with Space, select several parts and copy them, undo with Ctrl Z, walk through problems with F8, and line the map up with Tidy.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'Brain maps is a proper node editor'; docs/brain-maps.md 'Editing'

features.name: Build with AI
features.what: Describe a pipeline in a sentence and get a drafted map. The draft is repaired before you see it and saved only after you have looked at it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Build with AI drafts a map from a sentence'; [0.4.0] Fixed 'Brain maps drafted with AI arrive wired correctly'

features.name: Live activity
features.what: Each part shows what it did in the last 24 hours, and every setting says whether Studio reads it yet.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Brain maps show what they do'; docs/brain-maps.md 'Live activity'

features.name: Nested brains
features.what: An Another brain part hands a branch of the pipeline to another saved map, up to four levels deep.
features.evidence: docs/brain-maps.md 'Nested brains'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] Fixed 'a map that calls another brain'

features.name: Edits are never lost
features.what: Closing the editor keeps unsaved edits for next time. Discard unsaved changes throws them away when you mean to.
features.evidence: docs/brain-maps.md 'Closing the editor never asks and never discards'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0]

areas.summary: Read-only views of every coding session, its changes and evidence, Studio's own logs, and how your plans compare with the actual code.

features.name: Session explorer (E)
features.what: Every coding session, with checkpoints you can Reference, Explore, Restore or Expand. It also holds the always-on thread, the file-collision watch, the local auditor and the request inbox. Open task jumps to the task a session worked on.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The session explorer (E)'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Task run history… Open task'

features.name: Brief me and run controls
features.what: From the Explorer, ask the assistant for a briefing, pause or resume it, or kill a stuck run. The loop-guard switches live here too.
features.evidence: renderer/explorer.js 'Brief me', 'Kill this run' (Brief me present in v0.2.0); CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'The Explorer panel gains Memory alignment, Loop guard and Hold looping cards'

features.name: Activity & evidence (3)
features.what: A read-only view of the coding sessions: a feed of changes with diffs, totals per session, screenshots you can pin and the tail of the log.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'A-Eyes reads the OpenCode session store'; README.md 'Also in the box'

features.name: Trace
features.what: Studio's logs as channels in one viewer: the studio log, the assistant log, the run ledger, OpenCode's log and window warnings. Search, filter by level and source, follow live, copy or open the file.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Trace (Live, beside Activity)'; docs/architecture.md 'Trace'; renderer/trace.js

features.name: Analyzer (A)
features.what: Compares plans and notes with the current source, listing file:line evidence, missing references and completion claims nobody has verified. It runs locally, with an optional AI read.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'The Analyzer (A)'

features.name: Performance profiler
features.what: Records frame timings, rendering hotspots, host requests, CPU and memory, and exports them as JSON.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Performance profiler'; renderer/nav.js 'Performance profiler'

features.name: Pages that say what they mean
features.what: Pages leave out values that were never recorded instead of printing '?' or 'undefined', counts match what is shown, and errors read as plain sentences.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Menus say what they mean'; commits d77ff4e, 9a1b9f9

areas.summary: Compare models before you choose, see how they actually did on your own work, and track what each provider has used. Values that were never reported stay unknown instead of being shown as zero or free.

features.name: Model catalog (1)
features.what: Compare models by published quality, cost per request, requests per 5 hours, context size and monthly pool. Search with /, refresh with R, or print to PDF.

features.name: Catalog insights
features.what: A value map of cost against quality, a 'Where should I use it?' ranking, a heatmap of which models fit which tasks, and plan capacity pools.
features.evidence: booklet.template.html 'Catalog insights', 'Where should I use it?', 'Task fit heatmap'

features.name: Performance (2)
features.what: Measured speed, errors and reported cost of each model on your own project, filterable by task type. Opening it never runs paid measurements.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Model Lab and routing'; booklet.template.html 'Performance on your work'

features.name: Usage
features.what: Recorded calls by day, provider and model, kept apart from live account readings. Calls on plans that report no price are shown as unpriced, not free.

features.name: Provider accounts
features.what: Live plan limits and balances for OpenCode Go, z.ai, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway and LM Studio. Claude Code, Codex, Grok and Antigravity are read through their own logins without sending a prompt. From 0.4.5 there is one row per login.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'The Usage popover covers every provider'; docs/architecture.md 'Usage tracker'; [Unreleased] 'Each login gets its own row'

features.name: Usage popover
features.what: A pill in Command's corner shows your main plan's usage. Open it for one card per plan with reset times, balances and today's calls.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'The Usage popover'; docs/architecture.md 'The compact version is the Usage popover'

features.name: Context
features.what: Preview what a task's brief would carry within a budget of 1,000 to 8,000 tokens, and see what gets shortened.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Context previews the current task brief'; booklet.template.html 'Context preview'

features.name: What each model is good at
features.what: Model strengths are learned from verified wins and losses for each kind of work and shown in Agents routing and as a line in Vibe's Team. Learning can draw on this project, all projects or a blend.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.4] 'Model outcomes now retain their project'; renderer/autonomy-ui.js 'What each model is good at', 'Win estimate'

areas.summary: One menu, one search box and single-key shortcuts reach every page. Each section keeps its own Back and Forward history, and nothing you type is lost when you move around.

features.name: The menu
features.what: One menu down the left edge with Home, Work and Agents. New task and Search sit above them and Settings and Help below, with recent tasks for this project and a Keep menu open option.
features.evidence: README.md 'The menu down the left edge'; docs/architecture.md 'One menu down the left edge'; CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'One navigation rail replaces three menus'

features.name: Back and Forward per section
features.what: Each section keeps its own Back and Forward history. Selections, drafts and scroll positions survive ordinary navigation.
features.evidence: docs/unified-studio.md 'Navigation and overflow'

features.name: Search Studio (Ctrl K)
features.what: Find any page, tool, setting, action, task, node or model in everyday words. Results are grouped by menu section and open the real control.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.3] 'Search Studio'; docs/architecture.md glossary 'Search Studio'

features.name: Shortcuts sheet (?) and single keys
features.what: H goes Home (or Vibe), D opens Command, T Tasks, P Plans, I Ideas, B Brain maps, J Agent brain, E Sessions, A Analyzer and O Overhead. 1, 2 and 3 open the catalog, Performance and Activity, 4 or Ctrl , opens Settings and U opens Appearance. ? lists them all and Esc closes the current layer.
features.evidence: renderer/nav.js registry keys; README.md 'Also in the box'; GETTING_STARTED.md §5

features.name: Configuration (Ctrl Shift ,)
features.what: Every setting in one searchable tree, filed by what it does, opening the real control. It includes an Interface scale from 70% to 150%.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Configuration'; renderer/config-dialog.js (absent from v0.4.4 tree; restored by dc85f68)

features.name: Projects panel (M+)
features.what: M+ at the top of the menu lists your project folders, with + to add one. From 0.4.5 keyboard focus lands on the project you are in.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.3.0] 'The rail's M+ opens the project panel'; [Unreleased] 'M+ opens Projects on the selected project'

features.name: Classic navigation

features.what: Seven stops: scan, workspace, first map, connections, create, monitor and review. Walk with me opens the real menu and highlights the control, and the walkthrough remembers your place.
features.evidence: README.md 'First launch'; GETTING_STARTED.md 'The walkthrough'; CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] 'Seven-stop Start here walkthrough'

features.name: Launch screen and picking up where you left off
features.what: Choose a project, then Open studio (agents off) or Open and start agents. After a crash or an update restart, Studio reopens the folder and restarts the agents that were running.

features.name: Menus that move calmly
features.what: Rows that stay in place keep still or glide to their new position, new rows rise in, and panels slide in from the side you came from. Reduced motion turns this off.

features.what: Lists fade at the edges and show arrows on hover where there is more to see. Wheel, touch and keyboard scrolling all still work.

features.name: Ctrl R keeps your place
features.what: Reloading saves your view, selection and typed text first.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG.md [0.4.0] Fixed 'Ctrl R keeps your place'

features.name: Editor keys
features.what: In Vibe, Enter talks and Ctrl+Enter builds. On Home, Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line, and in Plans, Enter moves to the next field. Brain maps: F fits, Space searches parts, Ctrl F finds, Ctrl Z undoes, F8 walks problems and ? shows the legend. Project map: arrows select, Shift+arrows pan, Home fits, / searches and Backspace goes up.
features.evidence: booklet.template.html hints; docs/brain-maps.md 'Editing'; docs/architecture.md 'Project map', 'Planning'

notes:
Scope and sources: this covers only the working-with-agents scope. Community, Friends, Rooms, Listen together, music/media, colour themes, PC sync and the vault are left out, except where they touch agents (cowork file claims, node styles in Command). Local HEAD equals origin/main (6c1c940). The working tree has uncommitted edits in 13 renderer files from another session, so I read those files with git show origin/main, not from disk.

How to read 'since':
- '0.2.0' means the feature was in the first public release. History before 2026-09-19 is not recorded, so it may be older.
- 'coming-0.4.5' items are all under CHANGELOG [Unreleased] and/or in git log v0.4.4..origin/main (73 commits).

Release trap for the website:
- Commits 5d47154 (Configuration, Habits, menu motion) and 27413e2 (companion as pet/friend, six-bubble menu) are ancestors of the v0.4.4 tag.
- Their files were dropped by the 16:57 merge (65703a6) and restored after the tag in dc85f68, whose message says '0.4.4 was built without them'. The v0.4.4 tree has no renderer/config-dialog.js, renderer/motion.js, scripts/habits.cjs or scripts/companion-pet.cjs.
- The CHANGELOG lists them under Unreleased. Mark them coming-0.4.5; do not infer 'released' from commit ancestry.

Statuses the schema has no slot for (all planned, none built):
- Model Lab 'Compare models on one brief': a hidden tab marked Planned (booklet.template.html #model-lab-compare).
- The fleet overhaul (docs/fleet-overhaul-plan.md, approved 2026-09-27):
  - Live › Fleet 'branches' view with seats, pods, Health and a seat inspector (key F).
  - Work › Tasks lanes per agent, with a budget governor, Inbox/Deferred/Archived/Completed buckets and 'Message this agent'.
  - Missions and Refocus in Plans.
  - Docked panels and a status bar.
  - Seat recaps, a seat editor and team spec export/import.
  - Per-run token and cost metrics and budgets.
  - Your PCs and friends as hosts in the fleet.
- The plan says Phase 1 is 'in progress on fleet/overhaul', but no such branch exists locally or on origin.
- 0.4.0 roadmap leftovers (docs/roadmap-0.4.0.md status table): node-style done/absorb choreography in Agent brain and child sessions drawn on the Command tree are 'waiting'.

Statuses I did use:
- 'experimental': built but off by default or opt-in (ask_desk tool, nested delegation, head drafts, worktree runs). Policy Lab and the Jev shadow classifier are observation-only internals and are left out.
- 'rolling-out': cowork file claims. They need the rooms hub URL and a Discord link app ID, entered once per PC under Settings › Community › Connection details (0.4.5).

Naming the wiki should use:
- 'Session explorer' (key E) appears as 'Sessions' under Agents › Live.
- 'Feature ideas' (key I) is the Ideas page.
- 'Model Lab' is the old name for Performance, Usage and Context.
- 'Agent brain' (J) appears as 'Pipelines' in Agents › Live; Playbook and Project map sit under Agents › Workflows.
- Vibe's composer buttons are 'Talk it over' and 'Build it'. Build's Home composer uses 'Chat' and 'Create task'.

Stale doc spots found while reading (worth fixing in the wiki):
- GETTING_STARTED.md §2 still sends people to Settings › Connections and Models. The README and docs/unified-studio.md say connections, routing and roles live in Agents › Setup.
- GETTING_STARTED.md 'Review the defaults' and §1 still describe 'Auto build on by default / Verify first'. The real control is now the four permission modes, with Auto as the default; Auto build only moves between them.

Evidence convention: CHANGELOG sections are cited as [version] plus the entry's opening words; template means renderer/booklet.template.html on origin/main.
